Spec amendments: 2 need your call - from the spec review; applying as recommended reopens no tasks; no phase change.

1. Share retry policy - move retry policy into one owner. Adapters currently disagree about when to retry.
   This is a human call because changing who owns retries is an architecture choice.
   Example: adapter-local retry limits -> one coordinator retry limit
   Reviewer: changing retry ownership needs a human architecture choice
   Impact: Design / retries: each report adapter decides its own retries -> the existing report coordinator decides retries for every adapter, and adapters still run the reports
   A) accept - a new retry service owns all retry policies
   B) alt-1 - the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - the existing coordinator keeps retry policy consistent without adding a new service

2. Classify blocked execution - classify exit 126 as blocked rather than failed. Operators need to tell a launch problem apart from a report failure.
   This is a human call because it changes a status that operators see.
   Example: exit 126 = failed -> blocked
   Reviewer: operator-visible status changes need a human decision
   Impact: Design / run status: a run that exits with 126 counts as failed -> a run that exits with 126 counts as blocked
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - a separate status identifies launch failures

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
crosscut: Design / retries - old: each report adapter owns its retry policy -> new: a new retry service owns all retry policies (alt-1: the existing report coordinator owns the shared retry policy; adapters keep execution)
exit126: Design / run status - old: exit 126 is failed -> new: exit 126 is blocked

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs open each numbered item with a plain-words what/why sentence, list A) accept and B) alt-1 with one-line consequences on the crosscut item, give explicit letter recommendations with reasons, request one `<n>. <letter or free text>` line per item with bare `1` taking every recommendation, and include a human-call sentence per item (After's 'This is a human call because ...' phrasing is actually more direct than Before's 'so the reviewer left it to you'). Two things in After are worth tightening even though no fact catches them: the item-1 opening sentence dropped the concrete evidence Before carried ('alpha retries twice and beta retries four times'), and the Details line for crosscut now shows 'new: a new retry service owns all retry policies' with alt-1 parenthesised, which contradicts the Impact line and the Recommended: B that both point to the coordinator. Keep After's human-call phrasing, but have the Details new-state follow the recommended option (or label it 'accept: ... / alt-1: ...' symmetrically) and keep the evidence clause in the opening sentence so the menu stays internally consistent.
